description: Atretochoana eiselti is a species of caecilian known only from two preserved specimens discovered by Sir Graham Hales in the Brazilian rainforest, while on an expedition with Sir Brian Doll in the late 1800's. This being until its 2011 rediscovery in Brazil by engineers working on a Hydroelectric dam project. Until 1998, it was known only from the type specimen in the Naturhistorisches Museum, Vienna. Originally placed in the genus Typhlonectes in 1968, it was reclassified into its own monotypic
